imageryLayers.label: Total magnetic intensity
imageryLayers.guide: Colour differences show changes in the magnetic response of rocks. They can help trace rock units and structures, but do not directly show gold.

imageryLayers.label: Reduced-to-pole magnetics
imageryLayers.guide: Processing shifts magnetic anomalies closer to their likely source, making geological patterns easier to compare.

imageryLayers.label: Magnetic first vertical derivative
imageryLayers.guide: This emphasises rapid magnetic changes and can sharpen contacts, faults and shallow structures. Strong colour does not mean mineralisation.

imageryLayers.label: Radiometric imagery
imageryLayers.guide: Red represents relatively higher potassium, green higher thorium and blue higher uranium. Mixed colours show combinations. Surface cover, moisture and land disturbance can affect the response.

imageryLayers.label: Bouguer gravity
imageryLayers.guide: Colour changes indicate relative rock-density differences at depth and can reveal broad basins, intrusions and structures.

imageryLayers.label: Seismic C horizon
imageryLayers.guide: Colours represent the mapped seismic horizon values supplied by the official service. Use this for broad subsurface context, not as a commodity indicator.
